newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares end week mixed in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares end week mixed in Beirut.

text.p: Bank shares were mixed in the week ended on Friday on the Beirut Stock Exchange and brokers expected Bank Audi to continue a price rally at a slower pace.
Audi rose to $16.5 from $16.125 last week and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce steady at $12.
Shares in Audi began trading at $15 on January 20 while BLC shares first traded at $11.25 on December 30.

"Nothing has been more appealing on the market during the past two weeks than Audi shares which are expected to continue the trend upwards in the coming days but at a slower pace before settling down around a certain price," a broker, who wished not to be identified, said.
Solidere A shares -- distributed to former holders of property rights in the Beirut central district Solidere is rebuilding -- fell to $10.5 from $10.75.
B shares -- issued in a $650-million subscription in January 1994 -- rose to $11.25 from $11 last Friday.
"There has been huge supply on A shares with property right holders eager to sell theirs in one shot. Buy orders have been executed partially because there was not enough demand," the broker added.

Piping maker Eternit shares traded on Thursday and Friday at $1.5625 and $1.625 respectively, down from $1.75 on January 7 when they had last traded. A total of 12,000 Eternit shares were traded during the two days.
"Demand on Eternit shares was not huge enough to indicate real interest in the share. I think it was a special case of one interested buyer," the broker said.
Total weekly turnover in all traded shares on the BSE was 495,153 shares from 567,427 last week. Total value of shares traded on the floor rose to $5,979,464 from $6,974,064.
There was no trade in the three other firms listed on the BSE: Uniceramic, Ciments Libanais and Ciments Blancs.
The BLOM stock index rose on the week by 0.12 percent to 919.38 while the LISPI share index fell 0.53 percent to 81.16.
